issue.title: Add goto_charge mode value for L15 Ultra robot vacuum (oaelsi57ejdiavfh)
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds the missing `goto_charge` value to the `mode` datapoint (dp 4) for the L15 Ultra robot vacuum (category `sd`, product id `oaelsi57ejdiavfh`), following up on #643.

The cloud `function` list only declares `smart`, `zone`, `pose` and `part` for `mode`, but the device reports `goto_charge` on `mode` when it returns to its dock. Home Assistant logs this each time:

`Found invalid ENUM value 'goto_charge' for datapoint 'mode' in product id 'oaelsi57ejdiavfh', expected one of ['smart', 'zone', 'pose', 'part']`

The quirk redeclares the full `mode` range, including the existing four values, in the same `DeviceQuirk` chain as the `cistern` fix.

## Test plan

- Added `test_mode_enum_extended`, which checks `goto_charge` is absent from `device.function["mode"]` without the quirk and present with it. The existing fixture already has this device's `function` list, so no new fixture was needed.
- Loaded the updated quirk as a custom quirk on Home Assistant 2026.11.0, reloaded Tuya, sent the robot back to its dock, and the `goto_charge` warning no longer appeared.

## Related issue

"Fixes #734"

comment.body:
Thanks! The fix looks good, and it's great that you confirmed the warning is gone.

One thing to check: Home Assistant also shows `mode` as the vacuum's **Mode** select entity, so `goto_charge` now appears there as an option. As it isn't in the product's cloud definition, the cloud may reject it when it's chosen from Home Assistant. Could you try selecting `goto_charge` in that select and let us know what happens?

- **If the vacuum heads back to its dock**, that's a useful extra, and we can add a translated name for the option in Home Assistant Core.
- **If the command is rejected** (look for `2008` in the logs), please add a line to the quirk's docstring saying so, so the next person knows.

We're holding quirk merges until the second 2026.11 patch release, so I've moved this to draft in the meantime. Please mark it as ready for review once you've tested it.

labels.name: repo-0ea502d5

comment.body:
Sorry for the slow reply! Here's where this stands. Nobody is working on it at the moment, and it needs more than a quirk.

`rs` is Tuya's water heater category, which Home Assistant shows as a climate entity, so the temperature part is expected. The water-level datapoints (101–119) aren't declared by the cloud, so Home Assistant ignores them. A quirk could add them, but Home Assistant Core doesn't create any sensors for `rs` yet, so it would also need a Core change to show the water level and alarms.

To get started, we'd need:

1. **Which values matter most to you?** For example the water level, the low/high level limits and the level alarm. Adding a few well-understood datapoints is much easier than all 19.
2. **Their ranges and units:** your property dump shows the values, but not the ranges, scales or units. Is the water level a percentage (0–100), and are the temperatures in tenths of a degree (for example `550` = 55.0 °C)? The Tuya app's device page, or Tuya's thing model for the device, would show this.

If you're up for it, the [missing entities recipe](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/tuya-device-handlers/blob/main/docs/unsupported-category-or-dpcode.md) explains the two parts: a quirk here, and a Core PR for the entities.

issue.title: Invalid ENUM value hot for mode (and level_4 for fan_speed_enum) – product id f3goccgfj6qino4c

labels.name: repo-0ea502d5
labels.description: This requests support for a new device

issue.body:
Air conditioner (climate entity) reports values not in the expected enum.

Product id: f3goccgfj6qino4c
Airton brand

Home Assistant log (WARNING, tuya_device_handlers.type_information):
- Found invalid ENUM value `hot` for datapoint `mode`, expected one of ['auto', 'cold', 'wet', 'heat', 'fan']
- Found invalid ENUM value `level_4` for datapoint `fan_speed_enum`, expected one of ['auto', 'low', 'low_mid', 'mid', 'mid_high', 'high', 'mute', 'turbo']

Effect: after setting hvac_mode to `heat` from HA, the climate entity stays on `heat_cool` (auto), so heat mode is never shown as active.

Expected: `hot` should be mapped to heat (and `level_4` to a fan speed).
Happy to provide diagnostics privately or test a quirk.

comment.body:
Thanks for the report! The cloud declares `heat` for `mode`, but your AC reports `hot`, and it reports `level_4` for the fan speed, which isn't in the declared list either. A quirk can map these, but we need a bit more information first:

1. **Diagnostics:** please attach them here (**Settings → Devices & services → Tuya → your device → ⋮ → Download diagnostics**). They're safe to share publicly. They don't include your Tuya login or tokens, or the device's local key or IP address. They do include the device's Tuya id, which can't be used without your account, the names you gave the device and its entities, your Home Assistant version, and the device's datapoints and current values, which is what we need. You can open the file in a text editor to check before posting, or rename the device first if its name is personal.
2. **Fan speeds:** which fan speeds does the Tuya app offer, and which one makes the device report `level_4`? Changing the speed in the app with [debug logging](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/troubleshooting/#debug-logs-and-diagnostics) enabled for the Tuya integration will show the values it reports.

The desk doesn't accept a target height, so setting one would mean starting the motor and stopping it based on reports that travel through the Tuya cloud. If a report is late or lost, the desk would keep moving, which isn't safe to build into the integration.

The height sensor in Core is still worth doing. For the moving-to-a-height part, the [community forum](https://community.home-assistant.io/) is the best place to get help with a script or automation, such as stopping slightly before the target to allow for the delay.

issue.title: Found invalid ENUM value `weak` (<class 'str'>) for datapoint `suction`

labels.name: repo-0ea502d5
labels.description: This requests support for a new device

comment.body:
Thanks for the report and the diagnostics! The cloud only declares `strong` and `normal` for `suction`, but your vacuum reports `weak` too. A quirk can add the missing value. Could you try this as `<config>/tuya_quirks/sd_idr6emlmffa6pehv.py`, then reload the Tuya integration?

```python
"""Quirk for TESLA Electronics robot vacuum (product_id idr6emlmffa6pehv).

The cloud function list omits `weak` for the `suction` datapoint, but the
device reports it. Redeclare the full enum range so Home Assistant accepts
the value.
"""

from tuya_device_handlers import TUYA_QUIRKS_REGISTRY
from tuya_device_handlers.builder import DeviceQuirk
from tuya_device_handlers.const import DPMode

(
    DeviceQuirk()
    .applies_to(product_id="idr6emlmffa6pehv")
    .add_dpid_enum(
        dpid=14,
        dpcode="suction",
        dpmode=DPMode.READ | DPMode.WRITE,
        enum_range=["strong", "normal", "weak"],
    )
    .register(TUYA_QUIRKS_REGISTRY)
)
```

Once it's loaded, please check:

1. The warning no longer appears.
2. `weak` now shows up as a fan speed for the vacuum. Does choosing it from Home Assistant work? As it isn't in the product's cloud definition, the cloud may reject it with error `2008`.

If it works, you're welcome to open a pull request with the quirk and your diagnostics as the fixture. The [ENUM recipe](https://github.com/home-assistant-libs/tuya-device-handlers/blob/main/docs/adding-missing-enum-values.md) walks through it.

issue.title: [Feature request]: Support to set  height in regulable standing desk

comment.body:
Thanks for testing! Seeing both side by side helped. We'd rather not have two entities for the same value, and Core doesn't have a number for the desk height yet. As the desk doesn't accept a height, let's keep the **sensor only**, as in my last comment. Please drop the number from your changes before opening the PR.

In your screenshot the sensor is called "Distance": that's the default name for its device class. Once the `height` translation from `strings.json` is in Core, it will be called "Height".

For moving to a chosen height, the reports look fast enough in your screenshot, roughly 1 cm every half second. A script like this should stop within a centimetre or two of the target. The entity ids are examples, and the timeout is a safety stop:

```yaml
script:
  desk_to_height:
    fields:
      target:
        example: 100
    sequence:
      - variables:
          direction: >-
            {{ 'up' if target | float > states('sensor.mesa_height') | float else 'down' }}
      - action: select.select_option
        target:
          entity_id: select.mesa_up_down
        data:
          option: "{{ direction }}"
      - wait_template: >-
          {% set h = states('sensor.mesa_height') | float %}
          {{ h >= target | float if direction == 'up' else h <= target | float }}
        timeout: "00:01:00"
      - action: select.select_option
        target:
          entity_id: select.mesa_up_down
        data:
          option: stop
```

Please stay by the desk when you first try it.

issue.title: Add quirk for HQ-JS2326 humidifier (jsq, tfziezfrkj6s8frq)

labels.name: repo-0ea502d5
labels.description: This PR is ready for merge, and should no longer be amended

milestone.description: Quirks and changes for Home Assistant 2026.12. Due one week before the Core beta cutoff (last Wednesday of the month).

issue.body:
## Summary

Tuya advertises no datapoints for the HQ-JS2326 humidifier (`jsq`, product id `tfziezfrkj6s8frq`): `function`, `status_range`, `local_strategy` and `status` are all empty, so Home Assistant creates no entities.

This quirk adds the datapoints Home Assistant core maps for `jsq`, taken from the device's thing model (Tuya end-user API via tuya-smart-control-cli, `tuya device model <device_id> --json`):

| DP | Code | HA entity |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `switch_spray` | humidifier (power) |
| 13 | `humidity_set` | humidifier (target, 40-90 %, step 5) |
| 14 | `humidity_current` | humidifier (current) + humidity sensor |
| 16 | `sleep` | switch |
| 23 | `level` | select (`level_1`...`level_6`) |

Cloud codes are kept unchanged because commands are sent by DPCode.

**Limitation:** the Tuya cloud rejects every command for this product with `2008` (tested `switch_spray`, `humidity_set`, `sleep`, `level`: `{'code': '2008', 'success': False}`), so the entities are read-only in practice. As with #693, writable datapoints are still declared `READ | WRITE` and the limitation is documented in the quirk docstring.

The remaining thing-model datapoints (`switch_led` UV lamp, `countdown_left`, `fault` with `lack_water`, `time`, `switch_led_2`, `swing`, `clean_time`, `countdown_enable`, `set_time`, `switch_hun`) have no `jsq` mapping in core, so they are left out and listed in the docstring for a possible core follow-up.

Adds the first `jsq` quirk, so both `jsq/__init__.py` packages are new. Fixture is from the device's diagnostics with `id`, `terminal_id` and `home_assistant` removed.

## Test plan

- New tests: datapoints registered; HA default humidifier/select/sensor/switch definitions appear only with the quirk; commands use cloud codes; MQTT reports convert by dpId.
- `uv run pytest --cov tuya_device_handlers tests`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check src tests`, `pylint`, `codespell` all pass.
- Ran it as a custom quirk on HA 2026.11.0 (tuya-device-handlers 0.0.34): four entities created, live `humidity_current` reports update the sensor, commands rejected with `2008` as described.

## Related issue

None opened; device details are above. Same pattern as #740 / #741.

Drafted with help from Claude; I reviewed the code and description and tested on my own device.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01J7TDNb28EsWMGFB2HMNXT6

labels.name: repo-0ea502d5
labels.description: This PR is ready for merge, and should no longer be amended

milestone.description: Quirks and changes for Home Assistant 2026.12. Due one week before the Core beta cutoff (last Wednesday of the month).

issue.body:
## Summary

Adds a quirk for the July window air conditioner (`kt`, `KkdQFqwukvqeoKMa`, "Window Type Air Conditioner"). The cloud definition advertises `hot` in the `mode` enum, but this is a cooling-only unit, so Home Assistant offers a Heat mode the AC cannot perform. The quirk removes `hot` from the mode range (`auto`, `cold`, `wet`, `wind` remain).

It also adds ECO mode (DP 8) and sleep (DP 101). The device's thing model (Tuya end-user API, `/v1.0/end-user/devices/{id}/model`) declares them as writable booleans (`mode_ECO`, `sleep`), but the cloud doesn't advertise them to the sharing API. They're added under the standard `mode_eco` and `sleep` codes so HA can create Eco mode and Sleep switches once home-assistant/core supports them for `kt` (home-assistant/core#191161). `Fault` (DP 20) and `cf` (DP 102, temperature scale) are left out because HA doesn't use them for `kt` today.

## Test plan

- New fixture from my device's diagnostics (`id` / `terminal_id` removed) and tests showing the mode range before and after the quirk, the added ECO/sleep datapoints, and MQTT reports for DP 8 and DP 101 mapping to `mode_eco` / `sleep`. Full suite, ruff, ty, pylint, codespell and prettier pass locally.
- Loaded as a custom quirk on HA 2026.11.0: the climate entity's `hvac_modes` changed from `off, heat_cool, cool, heat, dry, fan_only` to `off, heat_cool, cool, dry, fan_only`.
- Real-device test of the ECO/sleep datapoints, together with home-assistant/core#191169 installed as a custom integration on HA 2026.11.0: the Eco mode and Sleep switches are created, and toggling ECO in the Tuya app updates HA within seconds via MQTT (DP 8 mapped to `mode_eco`). Writes from HA are rejected by the Tuya cloud ("The Tuya cloud rejected the command"), as expected for datapoints missing from the product's cloud function list, so these are effectively read-only on this device.

## Related issue

Related: home-assistant/core#191161

https://claude.ai/code/session_01J7TDNc6beu7eeivzWBPg82

## Proposed change

Add support for the existing `phase_1` through `phase_20` Raw DPs on Tuya multi-channel electricity meters. Each exposed channel uses the child-device architecture merged in #182161 and provides current, active power, voltage, reactive power, apparent power, and power factor through the existing Raw wrappers. Single-channel meters keep their sensors on the parent device.

The lookup uses one loop and shares the same stable channel identifiers as `phase_sN`. Existing `phase_a/b/c` and hex-string decoding remain covered by regression tests.

Validation: 208 Tuya tests and 3,050 snapshot assertions passed. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, Mypy and Pylint. The repository-wide hook run was interrupted; it is not reported as passed.

The Raw tests convert the bytes of the captured fixtures from #182848 into Tuya's base64 Raw representation. They verify 20 child devices, six available sensors per child, decoded values, single-channel behavior and stable identities after reload. This is an encoding-conversion unit test, not a newly captured Raw-product fixture or a live validation of PID `nazpxescctua1cll`.

This draft is ready for human review; a genuine Raw-product diagnostic fixture remains to be captured before requesting merge.

comment.body:
> @epenet Two updates since our last exchange.
> 
> First, I checked with our product team: current products are either Raw-only or String-only. There is no product that reports both phase_N and phase_sN. The dual-format case I mentioned earlier came from an older panel compatibility scenario, not a current product. So the selection-order edge case you raised shouldn't occur in production; the Core approach with both codes in one description still covers both product types.
> 
> Second, on the fixture: nazpxescctua1cll is a test-only PID; there is no physical device with that PID. The shadow diagnostic uses the same DP schema and goes through the same cloud and HA reporting and parsing path as a real device, but the readings are injected rather than measured by firmware.
> 
> Would you accept a shadow diagnostic as a temporary fixture for the indexed phase work, or do you need a capture from a physical device during normal reporting? If it's the latter, I'll wait for hardware and won't open the functional PR until then.
> 
> We also have a diagnostic from a real breaker that reports Raw phase_a/b/c. It uses the same ElectricityData parser, so it can serve as real-device evidence for the three-phase path, but it has no indexed phase_N DPs. I can share it separately if useful.

It's better to have real fixtures from normal reporting, not theoretical fixtures.
Replacing an existing theoretical one with a real one is of great benefit, and can be a standalone PR.

review.body:
Thanks for adding the action enums to Indevolt! The enums themselves look good.

Could you please remove the inline comments added on almost every changed line (`# Keep the existing charge handler.`, `# Shared key.`, `# Use the schema key.`, `# Match services.yaml.`, …)? They restate what the code already says, which the [code guidelines](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_guidelines) ask us to avoid, and without them the two `async_register` calls can go back to one line each.

issue.body: ### The problem After updating the custom integration [skye-harris/hass_local_openai_llm](https://github.com/skye-harris/hass_local_openai_llm) from HACS to version 1.15.0 I realized, that it was broken and that it also stated in their release notes, it needs Home Assistant 2026.11.0 for that version. I was only on Home Assistant 2026.10.4 though. I should not have been able to install that update in the first place, so I opened a ticket over there: [144](https://github.com/skye-harris/hass_local_openai_llm/issues/144). Turns out, they stated a minimal version in `hacs.json`, but only as a two-part semver: `2026.11`. ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? 2026.10.4 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? _No response_ ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue _No response_ ### Link to integration documentation on our website _No response_ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? ```txt ``` ### Additional information I found some documentation about how Home Assistant and Marketplace compare versions: https://contributors.home-assistant.io/marketplace/reference/hacs-json/#versions https://github.com/ludeeus/awesomeversion and this Live Demo, that shows what could possibly be the culprit here: https://awesomeversion.ludeeus.dev/ That's why I opened the issue here and not over at the hacs repository. If that's wrong I'll move it, it happened to me on Home Assistant 2026.10.4 so technically before it became Marketplace.

comment.body:
The problem in HACS (for <=2026.10.4) is already fixed in the old HACS repo, but it will never get released for those old HA versions.

It should not an issue with the new marketplace (>=2026.11): the installs will be blocked correctly.

issue.title: Add action enums to LIFX integration
issue.body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Add `LIFXService` and `LIFXServiceArgument` enums for the LIFX action names and action fields, replacing the integration's `SERVICE_*` and `ATTR_*` constants. The values are the same, so there is no functional change.

- The enums are in `const.py` because `services.py`, `manager.py` and `light.py` all use them.
- `LIFXServiceArgument` covers every field listed in `services.yaml`. Six of those were borrowed from the light platform and `homeassistant.const` before: `brightness`, `brightness_pct`, `color_name`, `rgb_color`, `mode` and `transition`.
- `effect_list` uses the `LIFXService` members, because selecting an effect on the light starts the action of the same name.
- Not replaced: 
  - `xy_color`, `hs_color` and `color_temp_kelvin` in the pulse schema, which are not in `services.yaml`
  - the fields `lifx.set_state` inherits from `LIGHT_TURN_ON_SCHEMA`
  - `ATTR_RSSI`, which is a sensor attribute.
- The old constants are removed. No custom integration in the HACS default list imports anything from `homeassistant.components.lifx` (checked against a snapshot of all 5,170 repositories taken on 2026-11-10), so nothing needs adding to #191544.

comment.body: Marked as draft as I want to triple-check some things relating to the mixing of various enums

review.body:
Thanks for adding the action enums to SMTP! A few role points:

- `smtp.send_message` is SMTP's own action, so its `title` and `message` fields would read better as `SMTPServiceArgument.TITLE` / `.MESSAGE` rather than `NotifyServiceArgument` (in the schema and the `smtp.send_message` test calls). The `notify.send_message` and legacy notify calls are right to use `NotifyServiceArgument`.
- `media_source`, `filename` and `content_id` are the keys inside each `attachments` item, not fields of the action itself, so they could stay plain constants (or a small enum for the attachment item) instead of `SMTPServiceArgument` members.
- `images` (and `html` on the legacy path) are keys of the legacy notify `data` payload rather than SMTP action arguments; keeping them as separate constants would avoid mixing the two roles.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Remove redundant coordinator data checks in the SMLIGHT update entity.

The firmware coordinator runs `async_config_entry_first_refresh` before `runtime_data` is set, so its `data` is always set when the update entities read it, and the data type implements neither `__bool__` nor `__len__`. The checks are always true and are removed; the radio index checks are kept.

Found while testing the `truthy-bool` mypy error code. Needed for #191236.
